Market Musings: Channel Position Backtest Study

Generated August 12, 2026 · Manual/on-demand deep-dive backtest, not part of daily automation · walk-forward, 25y lookback, 10y trailing regression window per sample · SPY / QQQ / XIC benchmarks

Study: Forward Returns From Channel Position

Walk-forward backtest, not in-sample: at each monthly sample date (up to 25 years of history per name), the regression is fit using only the trailing ~10 years of data available as of that date — no future prices — and R² ≥ 0.50, a positive slope, and positive trailing relative strength are all required at that date to count at all. That date is then classified Bottom (Z≤-1.5) / Middle / Top (Z≥+1.5) against its own trailing-only fit, and the name's real forward return is measured 6M/12M/3Y/5Y later. Because classification never sees the future, this is a fair walk-forward read of whether the setup has actually worked historically.
Across 9785 bottom-of-channel, 25417 middle-of-channel, and 1980 top-of-channel walk-forward observations (monthly-sampled, up to 25y lookback, R²≥0.50 names only, no look-ahead), Middle-of-channel had the best (or least-negative) median forward return relative to benchmark in 4 of 4 horizons measured. At 6M: -0.3% (Bottom), +0.1% (Middle), -1.2% (Top). By 5Y: -26.9% (Bottom), -16.2% (Middle), -28.3% (Top) — that edge erodes as the holding period lengthens, and neither channel extreme reliably beat sitting in the middle of an established trend.

Momentum Within the Middle

Restricted to Middle-band observations from the study above, split by whether that name's Z-score was Rising (recovering off the bottom) or Falling (fading off the top) over the trailing 63 trading days as of the sample date, using that same date's own trailing regression fit — no additional look-ahead. Answers: does a middle-of-channel name's recent direction of travel predict its forward return better than its static position does?
Restricting to the 25417 middle-of-channel observations at the 6M horizon (11818 with rising Z-score momentum over the trailing 63 trading days, 13599 with falling), median forward return relative to benchmark at 6M was -0.1% (Rising) vs. +0.3% (Falling); by 5Y it was -14.3% (Rising) vs. -18.0% (Falling) — suggesting recent Z-score momentum direction didn't reliably predict which forward relative return was better — mean reversion showed up about as often as continuation.

Bottom vs. Middle vs. Top: Is It Real, or Noise?

12 of 12 pairwise band comparisons (Bottom vs. Middle, Bottom vs. Top, Middle vs. Top, across all four horizons) came back statistically significant (95% bootstrap CI excludes zero) at the ticker level — take the band ordering from the Study section seriously, it survives clustering by ticker.
Ticker-level paired bootstrap (n=5000 resamples), not a test on the raw observation count: each ticker's many overlapping monthly samples are first collapsed to one mean relative return per band, so a ticker with both bands present contributes exactly one paired difference — the true independent sample size is the ticker count below, not the far larger raw row count in the Study section. "Significant" means the 95% bootstrap confidence interval on the mean paired difference excludes zero.
